title: SLI definition & prompt-set linked error budget policy for model rollouts
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: As we expand canary and progressive rollouts of new model versions (hosted and Dedicated), the runtime needs a clear mapping from measurable SLIs to rollout gating. Current latency-only SLOs don't capture semantic regressions introduced by model changes. This ticket defines a per-model SLI family that combines semantic-fidelity (prompt-set pass rates / metric thresholds) and latency tail behavior, and codifies an error-budget burn policy that ties directly to rollout percentage and automatic rollback/circuit-breaker decisions.

Goals:
- Define canonical SLI definitions for each model-endpoint pair: a semantic-fidelity measure derived from customer-facing prompt-sets, and a latency tail measure (p95/p99) weighted by route priority.
- Link SLI evaluation to rollout gates: specify error-budget burn thresholds that_pause_or_rollback rollouts, with clear mapping to progressive canary steps.
- Ensure multi-region failover and circuit-breaker interactions are defined (how an elevated burn in one region affects global rollout).
- Provide observability (Grafana dashboards), alert rules, and a short ops playbook for when a rollout triggers policy actions.

Scope: Per-endpoint/model SLI declarations + rollout gating policy + dashboard/alerts + runbook. Implementation touches: eval infra (prompt-set runner), runtime instrumentation, rollout controller logic, and alerting config.

Non-goals: Metric-level model retraining, design of new evaluation metrics (we will use existing prompt-set metrics and embedding similarity for now), changes to billing or plan tiers.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI schema file is added to infra-config that declares: semantic_fidelity_metric, semantic_thresholds (pass/fail), latency_metrics (p50/p95/p99) and weightings for each route.
Each production model has an associated prompt-set in the eval registry and a mapping entry in the SLI schema (documented in the Confluence page).

Rollout controller implements gating: if semantic_fidelity_pass_rate drops below configured threshold or error-budget burn rate exceeds X over Y minutes, the controller pauses and rolls back to previous version automatically.
Grafana dashboard shows per-model prompt-set pass rate trend, latency tails, and calculated error-budget remaining; alerts fire to PagerDuty on guardrail violations (severity mappings documented).
Runbook in Playbook repo with steps for oncall: how to validate regressions, temporary mitigations (route-level traffic split), and how to escalate to model owner and infra oncall.
implementation_notes:
Proposed approach: (1) Define SLI schema in infra-config repo (/configs/sli/model_rollouts.yml). (2) Add instrumentation: runtime emits per-request model_version, endpoint, prompt-set-id tag and latency quantiles; eval infra runs prompt-sets against release candidates and writes pass/fail to eval-store. (3) Rollout controller pulls SLI metrics (semantic pass rate + latency burn) from metrics pipeline and applies policy. (4) Alerts: implement thresholds in grafana/alertmanager; map to PD escalation.

Trade-offs considered:
- Using prompt-set pass-rate adds compute overhead for continuous evaluation; mitigated by sampling and batching nightly runs for low-traffic models.
- Embedding-similarity thresholds are brittle across model families; we will gate by absolute pass-rate on curated prompt-sets during rollout and evaluate moving to learned thresholds later.
- Immediate automatic rollback on first failure is conservative; we adopt progressive thresholds (canary pause -> pause+notify -> rollback at sustained burn).
rollout_plan:
1) Land SLI schema + example for 2 model endpoints (chat-small, embed-v2) behind feature flag. 2) Run daily prompt-set evaluation jobs and backfill dashboard for last 30 days. 3) Enable rollout controller for non-critical canaries (10% traffic) and observe for 1 week. 4) Expand to tier-1 models with staggered windows. 5) Postmortem and iterate on thresholds.

Gating policy (summary):
- Canary step sizes: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over minimum 6h windows.
- Soft pause: semantic pass-rate decrease >= 5 percentage points vs baseline OR p99 latency increase > 2x. Pause triggers a PagerDuty SEV2 notify.
- Hard rollback: sustained error-budget burn rate > 3x baseline for 30m OR semantic pass-rate < critical threshold (e.g., 70%) for 15m. Auto-rollback executed by rollout controller.
- Multi-region: if one region breaches, reduce regional weight to 0 and divert to global fallback; global rollout paused if total error budget across regions exceeds allocated threshold.

security_notes: Because we evaluate customer prompt-sets, ensure PII is redacted before storing prompt results in eval-store. Key management for eval-store is covered under KMS integration ticket. Security review required before enabling for private deployments.
